goal: Make block I/O errors (inaccessible blocks directory or files) fail consistently instead of being silently swallowed or crashing.
Stops the node from looking alive while being silently stuck unable to advance the chain, and makes P2P and RPC paths handle disk errors predictably.
reviewability: Paused: a fundamental Approach NACK about the error-handling design (nullptr vs exception-based translation) is unresolved and nobody has replied in 69 days.
Reviewing the current code risks being wasted if the project decides on a different error-handling strategy (raised as a meta-question by maflcko).
agreement: Disputed: josibake gave a formal Approach NACK arguing FlatFileSeq should preserve exceptions and translate them at the BlockManager boundary rather than collapsing into nullptr (josibake).
Author defends the consistency of the current minimal fix and disagrees this is the wrong direction (furszy).
Several reviewers gave positive/ACK reviews on the code and tests before the NACK (l0rinc, maflcko, rkrux, w0xlt, frankomosh, sedited).
maflcko posed an unanswered meta-question about whether the project even wants fatal-shutdown handling for these rare errors, suggesting the PR may need rework or closure.

categories.name: validation
why: P1 because a swallowed exception in ActivateBestChain previously left the node alive but permanently stuck, unable to process new blocks, without any visible error.
Fixing this closes a serious reliability gap in a validation invariant (chain must keep advancing), independent of the approach dispute over how errors should be modeled.

categories.name: p2p
why: P2 because GETDATA, GETBLOCKTXN and GETCFILTERS previously swallowed disk errors and left peers or the node in inconsistent states (unresponsive peer, inconsistent assert-vs-silent-catch behavior).
Making GETBLOCKTXN fatal and GETDATA disconnect-on-error improves message-handling correctness and liveness, though the benefit is narrower than the validation-side stuck-node fix.

categories.name: indexes
why: P3 because it converts an index code crash on an unexpected OpenFile exception into a silently ignored error, avoiding one crash class but not adding real index error handling.
Discussion flagged this as an incomplete, non-ideal interim fix with follow-up work explicitly deferred (index handling of file exceptions, RPC leaking filesystem errors).

categories.name: tests
why: P3 because the PR adds a reusable SimulateFileSystemError test utility that could be generalized for future fault-injection tests (noted by rkrux and l0rinc), beyond the area-specific tests it primarily contains.
Most of the added tests pin validation/p2p/indexes behavior rather than exercising general framework capability, so the leverage here is narrow.

result.summary: This PR makes block I/O error handling consistent across validation, P2P message handling, and indexes: GETDATA now disconnects the peer on disk error, GETBLOCKTXN triggers a fatal shutdown instead of an assert, ActivateBestChain triggers a fatal shutdown instead of silently swallowing an exception (previously leaving the node alive but stuck), GETCFILTERS logs through the expected error path, and index code no longer crashes on an unexpected filesystem exception. The vast majority of the diff (97% per the author) is new unit and functional test coverage reproducing each previously-mishandled scenario, plus a new SimulateFileSystemError test helper.
result.problem: Different code paths handled the same root cause (an inaccessible blocks directory or file) inconsistently: some correctly triggered a fatal shutdown, some silently swallowed the exception via a broad P2P catch-all leaving the node alive but permanently stuck reprocessing a failing block, some silently dropped P2P requests, and some crashed the node via assertions. This makes disk-related failures hard to diagnose and, in the worst case, leaves the node appearing healthy while it can no longer advance the chain.

open_concerns: josibake's Approach NACK: FlatFileSeq::Open should preserve the fs::filesystem_error exception and let BlockManager translate it at the right boundary, rather than collapsing it into the existing nullptr return used for all other Open() failures; author disagrees, arguing this would create two inconsistent error-signaling paths for the same failure class.

maflcko's unanswered meta-question: does the project actually want fatal-shutdown handling for these rare disk errors at all, and if so should it be done piecemeal or in one large coordinated PR (referencing overlapping PR #35676)?

w0xlt's concern about SimulateFileSystemError silently no-op'ing (false test coverage) on unsupported environments was partially addressed then reverted/reworked, and maflcko separately objected to the final ordering of rename-vs-chmod in the test helper as potentially masking failures.
resolved_concerns: Numerous test-nits and API cleanups (function naming, magic numbers, lock ordering under DEBUG_LOCKORDER, [[nodiscard]] on flatfile functions) were raised and fixed across many rounds by maflcko, l0rinc, rkrux, and w0xlt.
Whether ActivateBestChain's reorg path truly gets 'stuck' was questioned by sedited/rkrux; author clarified and adjusted description/tests accordingly.
Debate about whether to add [[nodiscard]] broadly was resolved by dropping that commit.

categories.name: indexes

categories.rationale: P2 because it fixes real inconsistencies in P2P request handling: 'GETDATA now... logs the error + disconnect the remote peer' and 'GETBLOCKTXN now triggers a fatal error' instead of an assert or silent swallow, per the PR description's enumerated cases 3 and 4.

categories.rationale: P1 because the description states the bug leaves a node 'alive but stuck, as subsequent block connections repeatedly attempt to process the failing block, throw the exception again, and get silently swallowed' with only a net-debug-level log most users never see, which is a serious reliability failure independent of the unresolved implementation-approach dispute.

result.card: This PR (furszy) makes block I/O error handling consistent across validation, P2P, and indexes: it fixes a scenario where ActivateBestChain silently swallows an exception and leaves the node 'alive but stuck' unable to advance the chain, makes GETDATA disconnect on disk error instead of silently dropping the request, replaces a GETBLOCKTXN assert with a graceful fatal shutdown, and stops index code from crashing on an unexpected filesystem exception. ~97% of the diff is new unit and functional test coverage reproducing each previously mishandled case. The problem is real and serious for validation (a node that looks healthy but can't process new blocks), but the PR is currently Paused: reviewer josibake issued a formal Approach NACK arguing the core fix (folding a filesystem exception into FlatFileSeq::Open's existing nullptr contract) is the wrong abstraction and should instead preserve the exception for translation at the BlockManager boundary, and maflcko's follow-up meta-question about whether the project wants this kind of fix at all has gone unanswered for over two months despite six earlier positive reviews (l0rinc, maflcko, rkrux, w0xlt, frankomosh, sedited). No hard PR dependencies block it, though it overlaps conceptually with #35676.
